title: The neighbour peel was proved — but never iterated into a product
content: The hard half of the Lovász Local Lemma induction step is a lower bound on the neighbour-block survival probability $\mu[\bigcap_{j\in S_1} A_j^c \mid C] \ge \prod_{j\in S_1}(1-x_j)$. The sibling **denominator-step** entry proved the SINGLE move behind it: $(1-x)\cdot l \le \mu[A^c \cap B \mid C]$ from $l \le \mu[B\mid C]$ and $\mu[A \mid B\cap C] \le x$ — peeling one neighbour $A = A_k$ deflates the running survival bound $l$ by a factor $(1-x_k)$. Its docstring explicitly deferred the rest: *'a well-founded recursion on $|S_1|$, still to be assembled'*. This entry assembles it. `cond_iInter_compl_ge_prod` is a `Finset.induction` over the neighbour block $S$ that iterates the peel — one insertion, one peel — accumulating the product $\prod_{j\in S}(1-x_j)$. The capstone `cond_failure_le_x_prod` then feeds the assembled product into the induction-step entry's abstract invariant, turning its abstract denominator $d$ into the concrete $\prod(1-x_j)$.
mathContext: ∏_{j∈S}(1 − xⱼ) ≤ μ[⋂_{j∈S} Aⱼᶜ | C], by induction on S iterating (1 − xₖ)·l ≤ μ[Aₖᶜ ∩ B | C].
relatedConcepts: well-founded recursion on a finite block

title: The recursion is a Finset.induction, one peel per insertion
content:
`cond_iInter_compl_ge_prod` proves $\prod_{j\in S}(1-x_j) \le \mu[ igcap_{j\in S} A_j^c \mid C]$ by `Finset.induction_on S`. The two side conditions the peel needs — positivity of every partial history $\mu[( igcap_{j\in T} A_j^c)\cap C] 
e 0$ and a per-event bound $\mu[A_k \mid ( igcap_{j\in T} A_j^c)\cap C] \le x_k$ — are quantified over **all** sub-blocks $T \subseteq S$, so the induction hypothesis inherits exactly the bounds it needs at the smaller block. **Base** $S=\varnothing$: $ igcap_{j\in\varnothing} A_j^c = 	ext{univ}$, so `cond_apply` + `Set.inter_univ` + `ENNReal.inv_mul_cancel` give $\mu[	ext{univ}\mid C]=1$ (using $\mu C 
e 0$ from the empty-block positivity), matching the empty product $\prod_\varnothing = 1$. **Step** `insert a s` ($a 
otin s$): `Finset.prod_insert` factors the product as $(1-x_a)\cdot\prod_s$, `Finset.set_biInter_insert` factors the survival set as $A_a^c \cap  igcap_{s} A_j^c$, and a single `mul_one_sub_le_cond_compl` — fed the induction hypothesis $\prod_s(1-x_j) \le \mu[ igcap_s A_j^c \mid C]$ — closes the goal. The identity $A_a^c \cap  igcap_s A_j^c =  igcap_{	ext{insert } a\, s} A_j^c$ is precisely why one peel advances the block by one element.
mathContext: Base: μ[univ | C] = 1 = ∏_∅. Step: (1 − xₐ)·∏_s ≤ μ[(A a)ᶜ ∩ ⋂_s Aⱼᶜ | C] = μ[⋂_{insert a s} Aⱼᶜ | C].

title: Threading the product into the invariant: the abstract d becomes ∏(1 − xⱼ)
content: `cond_failure_le_x_prod` is the payoff. The induction-step entry proved the invariant $\mu[A_i \mid N\cap C] \le x_i$ closes *once a denominator lower bound $d \le \mu[N\mid C]$ is supplied*, but left $d$ abstract. Here $d$ becomes concrete: set $C = \bigcap_{j\in S_2} A_j^c$ (measurable via `Finset.measurableSet_biInter`), obtain $\prod_{j\in S_1}(1-x_j) \le \mu[\bigcap_{j\in S_1} A_j^c \mid \bigcap_{j\in S_2} A_j^c]$ from `cond_iInter_compl_ge_prod`, and hand it to `cond_failure_le_x` as the denominator bound. Under the asymmetric LLL budget $\mu(A_i) \le x_i\cdot\prod_{j\in S_1}(1-x_j)$ and the non-neighbour independence $\text{IndepSet}\,A_i\,(\bigcap_{S_2} A_j^c)\,\mu$, the result is $\mu[A_i \mid (\bigcap_{S_1} A_j^c)\cap(\bigcap_{S_2} A_j^c)] \le x_i$ — the maintained invariant, now with the denominator equal to the actual product the textbook proof threads. **Honest scope:** the per-event bounds this consumes are themselves instances of the same invariant at smaller conditioning sets; the two directions form the Erdős–Lovász mutual recursion, and closing that mutual loop into an unconditional LLL is the remaining open OQ-01 target.
mathContext: cond_failure_le_x with d := ∏_{S₁}(1 − xⱼ) supplied by the recursion ⇒ μ[Aᵢ | (⋂_{S₁} Aⱼᶜ) ∩ (⋂_{S₂} Aⱼᶜ)] ≤ xᵢ.
